chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Baseer who said:

I was sitting in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when Umm Khalid, who had been cut off by Yusuf ibn Umar, came in and sought permission to see him. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Would it please you to hear her words?' I said: 'Yes'. He said: 'As for now, give permission to her.' And he made me sit on the settee with him.

Then she came in and spoke, and she was an eloquent woman. She asked him about the two of them. He said to her: 'Consider them as friends (Waliyyayn).' She said: 'So shall I say to my Lord when I meet Him that you have ordered me to befriend these two?' He said: 'Yes.' She said: 'This one who is with you on the settee orders me to be distant from them (Al-Bara'ah), and Kathir al-Nawwa' orders me to befriend them. So which of the two is better and more beloved to you?'

He said: 'This one is more beloved to me by Allah than Kathir al-Nawwa' and his companions. Indeed, this one debates by saying: "And whoever did not judge by what Allah revealed, those are they that are the unbelievers"; "And whoever did not judge by what Allah revealed, those are they that are the unjust"; "And whoever did not judge by what Allah revealed, those are they that are the transgressors".'

key_terms.أُمُّ خَالِدٍ: Umm Khalid, a companion known for her eloquence and theological discussions.
key_terms.الظَّالِمُونَ: The unjust, the second category mentioned.
key_terms.الْبَرَاءَةِ: Disengagement or enmity, the opposite of Wilayah.
key_terms.الْفَاسِقُونَ: The transgressors, the third category mentioned.
key_terms.الْكَافِرُونَ: The disbelievers, one of the three categories mentioned in the Quranic verses.
key_terms.تَوَلَّيْهِمَا: Make them your Wali (friend/ally/guardian), indicating love and allegiance.
key_terms.قَطَعَهَا: He cut off her link (to the Imams), meaning he severed her connection or status.
key_terms.كَثِيرٌ النَّوَّاءُ: Kathir ibn Abi al-Nawwa', a contemporary companion known for his specific theological views.
key_terms.يُخَاصِمُ: He debates or argues, indicating an active intellectual engagement.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Quranic verses cited by the Imam regarding judging by what Allah revealed?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the doctrine of *al-Wala' wa al-Bara'* (alliance and disavowal) through a dialogue between Imam al-Sadiq and Umm Khalid, who was exiled by Yusuf ibn Umar. The Imam distinguishes between the moderate stance of Kathir al-Nawwa' and the rigorous stance of the companion on the *tinfasa*, who grounds his disavowal in the Quranic triad of *Kufr*, *Zulm*, and *Fisq* for those who fail to judge by divine revelation. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on linking theological allegiance directly to the application of Quranic judgment in governance and belief.
